lots.what_it_is: About 40 pieces of English brown salt-glaze stoneware domestic or hotel ware: coffee pots, lidded hot-water jugs, graduated cream and milk jugs, a cheese or sardine type dish with pierced lid, loose lids. Upper half treacle or tan glazed, lower half sand-textured (shagreen) with a sprigged band. Style of Doulton Lambeth, Bourne Denby or Lovatt Langley hotel ware, c.1900-1950. No base or mark shown, so maker unconfirmed.
lots.score_reason: Plain banded domestic stoneware, not decorated Doulton art ware. Tasmanian sales of brown stoneware jug groups run about $20-140 hammer, the top being decorated Doulton Lambeth. A big unmarked lot of plain ware is likely $50-150 all up, and maker is unread.

lots.what_it_is: Box of about 14 small decorative glass pieces. Best piece is a dark green glass hookah (narghile) base, densely gilt with roundels and white enamel dots, Bohemian or Turkish style for the Middle Eastern market, probably mid 20th century rather than 19th. Also an orange cased vase, rainbow-swirl bowl, latticino ring-tree dish, two millefiori paperweights (one modern Chinese-type), a marigold carnival glass lid, a frosted green flower frog, a green miniature cup and saucer, a green bottle, a gilt-rimmed green bowl, a yellow frosted beaker and a blue frosted cup. No marks visible.
lots.score_reason: Mostly ordinary decorative glass; Gowans boxes of coloured or art glass sold $15-120. The hookah base is the only piece that might lift it, but no priced comparable for it was found and it looks like later tourist-grade work.
